exposure: Antihypertensive medication use (pre-pregnancy, during pregnancy, postpartum periods)
Specific types of antihypertensive medications (dihydropyridines, beta-blockers, Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers, vasodilators)
outcome: Patterns of discontinuing, continuing, switching, and initiating antihypertensive medications during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 2,030,821 pregnancies that resulted in a live birth in South Korea between 2013 and 2017, extracted from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment (HIRA) database.
finding: The prevalence of antihypertensive use during pregnancy in South Korea was 3.1%, with dihydropyridines being the most frequent medication type used (e.g., 40.7% in the first trimester, 89.7% in the third trimester), and 86.3% of women exposed during pregnancy were first-time users.
